title: A rotating protostellar jet launched from the innermost disk of HH 212
question: Does the HH 212 protostellar jet rotate, and if so, from what disk radius is it launched (does the jet remove angular momentum from the innermost disk)?

data.angular_resolution: Cycle 1 ~0.16" (64 AU); Cycle 3 0.02" (8 AU); tapered 0.06" (24 AU)
data.sensitivity: 1.6 mJy/beam (~40 K) at 0.02"; 1.9 mJy/beam (~6 K) at 0.06"

what.value: 350 GHz dust continuum map of the disk, overlaid

evidence.quote: on top of the dust continuum map (orange image) of the accretion disk at 352 GHz(cite: Lee2017)

a jet velocity(cite: Lee2015) of $v_j
\sim$ 115$\pm$50 km s$^{-1}$
With a protostellar mass of $M_\ast \sim$ 0.25$\pm$0.05 $M_\odot$(cite: Lee2014; Codella2014)

what.value: Jet inclination ~4 deg to plane of sky

evidence.quote: The jet, lying close ($\sim$ 4$^\circ$) to the plane of the sky(cite: Claussen1998)

recipe.goal: Image SiO jet at 8 AU and 24 AU
recipe.method: Cycle 3 only for 0.02" maps; Cycle 1+3 with 0.05" taper for 0.06" maps; natural weighting, 0.848 km/s channels
Gaussian fits to spatial profiles perpendicular to the jet axis, deconvolved by the 8 AU beam
PV diagrams cut across knots; emission peaks from Gaussian fits; linear least-squares fit; peak position errors = quarter FWHM; >7 sigma detections
key_parameters: Peak position uncertainty = a quarter of the FWHM

recipe.method: l = m (ΔV)^2/4 from gradient m and velocity range ΔV; mean excluding N3
assumptions: Jet rotation symmetric about knot center

recipe.method: Approximate analytic solution of magneto-centrifugal energy and angular momentum conservation (Anderson et al. 2003) with correction terms in eta
assumptions: Gravitational potential negligible at large distance, jet velocity much larger than rotation, inclination ~4 deg

answer_key.quantity: Specific angular momentum N2, N3, S3

evidence.quote: 9.4$\pm$1.0, 9.6$\pm$6.0, and 11.4$\pm$1.3 AU km s$^{-1}$ for knots N2, N3, and S3
the mean specific angular momentum is $l_j \sim 10.2\pm1.0$ AU km s$^{-1}$
the launching radius of the jet is estimated to be $r_\textrm{\scriptsize 0}\sim$ 0.05$_{-0.02}^{+0.05}$ AU
with a position angle measured to be $\sim$ 23$^\circ$

evidence.loc: Mean (or Systemic) Velocities of the Jet
evidence.quote: with a mean velocity of $\sim$ 4 km s$^{-1}$ LSR

not_stated_but_needed: Flux/passband/gain calibrator names (only in Supplementary tables not given)
